title.zh: 卷七十七 列傳第十五: 宗弼本名兀朮，子:亨(本名孛迭) 張邦昌 劉豫 昌本名撻懶
title.en: Volume 77 Biographies 15: Zong Bi formerly named Wupai, son: Heng (formerly named Beidie), Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Chang formerly named Talan
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第十五: 宗弼本名兀朮，子:亨(本名孛迭) 張邦昌 劉豫 昌本名撻懶 Volume 77 Biographies 15: Zong Bi formerly named Wupai, son: Heng (formerly named Beidie), Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Chang formerly named Talan

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五 ○宗弼本名兀朮，子:亨

translations.literal: Biographies 15 ○ Zongbi, original name Wuzhu, son: Heng
translations.idiomatic: Biography 15: Zongbi (original name Wuzhu), and his son Heng

sentences.zh: (本名孛迭)

translations.literal: (original name Beidie)
translations.idiomatic: (original name Beidie)

sentences.zh: 張邦昌 劉豫 昌本名撻懶

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Chang original name Talan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, and Chang (original name Talan)

sentences.zh: 宗弼，本名斡啜，又作兀朮，亦作斡出，或作晃斡出，太祖第四子也。

translations.literal: Zongbi, original name Wochuo, also written Wuzhu, also written Wochu, or written Huangwochu, was the fourth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi, whose original name was Wochuo—also recorded as Wuzhu, Wochu, or Huangwochu—was the fourth son of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 希尹獲遼護衛習泥烈，問知遼帝獵鴛鴦濼。

translations.literal: Xiyin captured the Liao guard Xini Lie and learned by inquiry that the Liao emperor was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin captured the Liao guard Xini Lie and learned from him that the Liao emperor was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh.

sentences.zh: 都統杲出青嶺，宗望、宗弼率百騎與馬和尚逐越盧、孛古、野裏斯等，馳擊敗之。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Gao came out through Qing Ridge; Zongwang and Zongbi led a hundred horsemen with Monk Ma in pursuit of Yuelu, Bogu, Yelisi, and others, charging to attack and defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: When Supreme Commander Gao advanced through Qing Ridge, Zongwang and Zongbi led a hundred horsemen with Monk Ma in pursuit of Yuelu, Bogu, Yelisi, and others, riding hard to rout them.

sentences.zh: 宗弼矢盡，遂奪遼兵士槍，獨殺八人，生獲五人，遂審得遼主在鴛鴦濼畋獵，尚未去，可襲取者。

translations.literal: Zongbi's arrows were exhausted, so he seized Liao soldiers' spears, alone killed eight men, captured five alive, and thereby ascertained that the Liao ruler was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh, had not yet left, and could be taken by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: When his arrows ran out, Zongbi seized spears from Liao soldiers, killed eight men single-handed, and took five alive. From this he confirmed that the Liao emperor was still hunting at Yuanyang Marsh and had not yet departed—a target that could be struck.

sentences.zh: 及宗望伐宋，宗弼從軍。

translations.literal: When Zongwang campaigned against Song, Zongbi followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang marched against the Song, Zongbi went with the army.

sentences.zh: 取湯陰縣，降其卒三千人。

translations.literal: He took Tangyin County and accepted the surrender of its three thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Tangyin County and accepted the surrender of three thousand of its troops.

sentences.zh: 至禦河，宋人已焚橋，不得渡，合盧梭以七十騎涉之，殺宋焚橋軍五百人。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yu River, the Song had already burned the bridge and he could not cross; with Helusuo he forded it with seventy horsemen and killed five hundred Song troops who had burned the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yu River the Song had already burned the bridge, blocking a crossing. With Helusuo he waded across at the head of seventy horsemen and killed five hundred Song troops who had set the bridge ablaze.

sentences.zh: 宗望遣吳孝民先入汴諭宋人，宗弼以三千騎薄汴城。

translations.literal: Zongwang sent Wu Xiaomin ahead into Bian to instruct the Song; Zongbi with three thousand horsemen pressed close to the walls of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang sent Wu Xiaomin ahead into Bian to parley with the Song, while Zongbi advanced on the city with three thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宋上皇出奔，選百騎追之，弗及，獲馬三千而還。

translations.literal: The Song retired emperor fled; he selected a hundred horsemen to pursue him, did not overtake him, seized three thousand horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired Song emperor fled, he took a hundred horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him; he seized three thousand horses and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宋主自揚州奔于江南，宗弼等分道伐之。

translations.literal: The Song emperor fled from Yangzhou to the lands south of the Yangtze; Zongbi and others campaigned against him by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor fled from Yangzhou into the south, and Zongbi and others pursued him along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 進兵歸德，城中有自西門北門出者，當海複敗之。

translations.literal: Advancing to Guide, those who came out of the city through the west and north gates were again defeated by Danghai.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Guide, he defeated Song forces that sallied from the west and north gates, with Danghai again routing them.

sentences.zh: 乃絕隍築道，列砲隍上，將攻之。

translations.literal: He then cut off the moat and built a causeway, arrayed cannon on the ramparts, and was about to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He then filled in the moat and built a causeway, set cannon on the ramparts, and prepared to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 城中人懼，遂降。

translations.literal: The people in the city were afraid and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the defenders surrendered.

sentences.zh: 先遣阿裏、蒲盧渾至壽春，宗弼軍繼之。

translations.literal: He first sent Ali and Puluhun to Shouchun; Zongbi's army followed after.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Ali and Puluhun to Shouchun, with Zongbi's army following close behind.

sentences.zh: 宋安撫使馬世元率官屬出降。

translations.literal: The Song pacification commissioner Ma Shiyuan led his officials out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Song pacification commissioner Ma Shiyuan led his staff out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 進降盧州，再降巢縣王善軍。

translations.literal: Advancing, he accepted the surrender of Luzhou and again accepted the surrender of Wang Shan's army at Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Luzhou, then accepted the surrender of Wang Shan's forces at Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 當海等破酈瓊萬余眾於和州，遂自和州渡江。

translations.literal: Danghai and others defeated Li Qiong's force of more than ten thousand at Hezhou, then crossed the river from Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Danghai and others routed Li Qiong's army of more than ten thousand at Hezhou, then crossed the Yangtze from there.

sentences.zh: 將至江寧西二十裏，宋杜充率步騎六萬來拒戰，鶻盧補、當海、迪虎、大抃合擊破之。

translations.literal: When about to reach a point twenty li west of Jiangning, the Song Du Chong led sixty thousand infantry and cavalry to resist; Helubu, Danghai, Dihu, and Daban jointly attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li west of Jiangning, the Song commander Du Chong met them with sixty thousand infantry and cavalry. Helubu, Danghai, Dihu, and Daban joined forces and broke his army.

sentences.zh: 宋陳邦光以江寧府降。

translations.literal: The Song Chen Bangguang surrendered Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bangguang surrendered Jiangning Prefecture to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 留長安奴、斡裏也守江寧。

translations.literal: He left Chang'annu and Woliye to garrison Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He left Chang'annu and Woliye to hold Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 使阿魯補、斡裏也別將兵徇地，下太平州、濠州及句容、溧陽等縣，溯江而西，屢敗張永等兵，杜充遂降。

translations.literal: He sent Alubu and Woliye with separate commands to subdue the region, taking Taiping Prefecture, Haozhou, and the counties of Jurong, Liyang, and others; going upriver westward they repeatedly defeated Zhang Yong's troops, and Du Chong thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Alubu and Woliye with separate detachments to overrun the region, capturing Taiping Prefecture, Haozhou, and counties including Jurong and Liyang. Moving up the Yangtze to the west, they repeatedly defeated Zhang Yong's forces, and Du Chong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 宗弼自江寧取廣德軍路，追襲宋主於越州。

translations.literal: Zongbi from Jiangning took the Guangde Army route and pursued the Song emperor to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangning, Zongbi marched by the Guangde Army route to pursue the Song emperor toward Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 至湖州，取之。

translations.literal: Reaching Huzhou, he took it.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Huzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 先使阿裏、蒲盧渾趨杭州，具舟於錢塘江。

translations.literal: He first sent Ali and Puluhun hurrying to Hangzhou and prepared boats on the Qiantang River.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Ali and Puluhun ahead to Hangzhou and had boats readied on the Qiantang River.

sentences.zh: 宗弼至杭州，官守巨室皆逃去，遂攻杭州，取之。

translations.literal: When Zongbi reached Hangzhou, officials, garrison troops, and great households had all fled; he then attacked Hangzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi reached Hangzhou, officials and wealthy families had already fled. He assaulted the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 宋主聞杭州不守，遂自越奔明州。

translations.literal: The Song emperor, hearing that Hangzhou could not be held, then fled from Yue to Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Hangzhou had fallen, the Song emperor fled from Yuezhou to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗弼留杭州，使阿裏、蒲盧渾以精兵四千襲之。

translations.literal: Zongbi remained at Hangzhou and sent Ali and Puluhun with four thousand picked troops to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi remained at Hangzhou and sent Ali and Puluhun with four thousand elite troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 訛魯補、朮列速降越州。

translations.literal: Elubu and Shuliesu accepted the surrender of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Elubu and Shuliesu took Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 大抃破宋周汪軍，阿裏、蒲魯渾破宋兵三千，遂渡曹娥江。

translations.literal: Daban defeated the Song army of Zhou Wang; Ali and Puluhun defeated three thousand Song troops, then crossed the Cao'e River.
translations.idiomatic: Daban routed Zhou Wang's Song force; Ali and Puluhun defeated three thousand Song troops and crossed the Cao'e River.

sentences.zh: 去明州二十五裏，大破宋兵，追至其城下。

translations.literal: Twenty-five li from Mingzhou, they inflicted a great defeat on the Song army and pursued to beneath its walls.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five li from Mingzhou they routed the Song army and pursued to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 城中出兵，戰失利，宋主走入於海。

translations.literal: The city sent out troops; the battle went badly and the Song emperor fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The city sallied but was beaten; the Song emperor escaped by sea.

sentences.zh: 宗弼中分麾下兵，會攻明州，克之。

translations.literal: Zongbi divided his troops in half and jointly attacked Mingzhou, capturing it.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi split his forces and converged on Mingzhou, which fell.

sentences.zh: 阿裏、蒲盧渾泛海至昌國縣，執宋明州守趙伯諤，伯諤言：「宋主奔溫州，將自溫州趨福州矣。」

translations.literal: Ali and Puluhun sailed the sea to Changguo County, seized the Song prefect of Mingzhou Zhao Boyi, and Boyi said: "The Song emperor has fled to Wenzhou and will go from Wenzhou toward Fuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Ali and Puluhun put to sea and reached Changguo County, where they seized Zhao Boyi, the Song prefect of Mingzhou. Boyi said, "The emperor has fled to Wenzhou and will head from there toward Fuzhou."

sentences.zh: 遂行海追三百餘裏，不及，阿裏、蒲盧渾乃還。

translations.literal: They then pursued by sea for more than three hundred li, did not overtake him, and Ali and Puluhun returned.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued by sea for more than three hundred li but could not overtake him, and Ali and Puluhun turned back.

sentences.zh: 宗弼還自杭州，遂取秀州。

translations.literal: Zongbi returned from Hangzhou and then took Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Hangzhou, Zongbi captured Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 赤盞暉敗宋軍於平江，遂取平江。

translations.literal: Chishanhui defeated the Song army at Pingjiang and then took Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chishanhui defeated the Song at Pingjiang and took the city.

sentences.zh: 阿裏率兵先趨鎮江，宋韓世忠以舟師扼江口。

translations.literal: Ali led troops ahead to Zhenjiang; the Song Han Shizhong with a fleet held the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Ali advanced first on Zhenjiang, where Han Shizhong blocked the river mouth with his fleet.

sentences.zh: 宗弼舟小，契丹、漢軍沒者二百餘人，遂自鎮江溯流西上。

translations.literal: Zongbi's boats were small; more than two hundred Khitan and Han soldiers were drowned, so he went upriver westward from Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi's boats were too small—more than two hundred Khitan and Han soldiers were lost—and he moved up the Yangtze westward from Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 世忠襲之，奪世忠大舟十艘，於是宗弼循南岸，世忠循北岸，且戰且行。

translations.literal: Shizhong attacked him; he seized ten of Shizhong's large ships, and thereafter Zongbi followed the south bank while Shizhong followed the north bank, fighting as they went.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong attacked, he captured ten of Shizhong's large warships. Thereafter Zongbi kept to the south bank and Shizhong to the north, fighting as they advanced.

sentences.zh: 世忠艨艟大艦數倍宗弼軍，出宗弼軍前後數裏，擊柝之聲，自夜達旦。

translations.literal: Shizhong's tower ships and great vessels were several times Zongbi's force; they extended several li before and behind Zongbi's army; the sound of night watches striking clappers lasted from night until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong's tower ships and great vessels outnumbered Zongbi's fleet many times over, stretching for miles ahead and behind. The clatter of night watches sounded from dusk until dawn.

sentences.zh: 世忠以輕舟來挑戰，一日數接。

translations.literal: Shizhong with light boats came to challenge; in one day there were several engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong sent light craft to skirmish, and there were several clashes in a single day.

sentences.zh: 將至黃天蕩，宗弼乃因老鸛河故道開三十裏通秦淮，一日一夜而成，宗弼乃得至江寧。

translations.literal: When about to reach Huangtiandang, Zongbi opened thirty li along the old course of the Laoguan River to connect with the Qinhuai, completing it in one day and one night, and thereby reached Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Near Huangtiandang, Zongbi reopened thirty li of the old Laoguan River channel to reach the Qinhuai, finishing the work in a single day and night. He thus escaped to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 撻懶使移剌古自天長趨江甯援宗弼，烏林答泰欲亦以兵來會，連敗宋兵。

translations.literal: Talan sent Yelagu from Tianchang hurrying to Jiangning to relieve Zongbi; Wulindatai also wished to come with troops to join, and they repeatedly defeated Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: Talan sent Yelagu from Tianchang to relieve Zongbi at Jiangning, while Wulindatai also marched to link up; together they repeatedly defeated Song forces.

sentences.zh: 宗弼發江寧，將渡江而北。

translations.literal: Zongbi set out from Jiangning, intending to cross the river and go north.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi left Jiangning intending to cross the Yangtze and withdraw north.

sentences.zh: 宗弼軍渡自東，移剌古渡自西，與世忠戰于江渡。

translations.literal: Zongbi's army crossed from the east and Yelagu crossed from the west, fighting Shizhong at the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi's force crossed from the east and Yelagu from the west, engaging Shizhong at the ford.

sentences.zh: 世忠分舟師絕江流上下，將左右掩擊之。

translations.literal: Shizhong divided his fleet to block the river above and below, intending to strike from both flanks.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong split his fleet to seal the river above and below, planning to envelop them from both sides.

sentences.zh: 世忠舟皆張五糸兩，宗弼選善射者，乘輕舟，以火箭射世忠舟上五糸兩，五糸兩著火箭，皆自焚，煙焰滿江，世忠不能軍，追北七十裏，舟軍殲焉，世忠僅能自免。

translations.literal: Shizhong's ships all spread double-layered awnings of five-ply silk; Zongbi selected skilled archers, boarded light boats, and with fire arrows shot at the five-ply silk awnings on Shizhong's ships; the awnings caught fire from the arrows and all burned of themselves; smoke and flames filled the river; Shizhong could not maintain his army; pursued north for seventy li, his fleet was annihilated; Shizhong barely escaped himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong's ships were rigged with double layers of silk awnings. Zongbi chose skilled archers in light boats who fired rockets at the awnings; they ignited and burned away, until smoke and flame filled the river. Shizhong's fleet was shattered. Pursued for seventy li, his navy was destroyed and Shizhong barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 宗弼渡江北還，遂從宗輔定陝西。

translations.literal: Zongbi crossed north of the river and returned, then followed Zongfu to pacify Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river to the north, Zongbi joined Zongfu in securing Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與張浚戰于富平。

translations.literal: He fought Zhang Jun at Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Zhang Jun at Fuping.

sentences.zh: 宗弼陷重圍中，韓常流矢中目，怒拔去其矢，血淋漓，以土塞創，躍馬奮呼搏戰，遂解圍，與宗弼俱出。

translations.literal: Zongbi was trapped in a heavy encirclement; Hanchang was struck in the eye by a stray arrow, angrily pulled out the arrow, blood streaming down, stuffed the wound with earth, leaped on his horse shouting fiercely and fought, thereby broke the encirclement, and both he and Zongbi got out.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi was caught in a tight encirclement. Hanchang took an arrow in the eye, wrenched it out in fury—blood streaming—and packed the wound with earth. Mounting again, he charged shouting and broke the ring, bringing both himself and Zongbi out alive.

sentences.zh: 既敗張浚軍于富平，遂與阿盧補招降熙河、涇原兩路。

translations.literal: Having defeated Zhang Jun's army at Fuping, he then with Alubu accepted the surrender of the Xihe and Jingyuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Zhang Jun at Fuping, he and Alubu accepted the submission of the Xihe and Jingyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 及攻吳玠于和尚原，抵險不可進，乃退軍。

translations.literal: When attacking Wu Jie at Heshangyuan, they reached difficult terrain and could not advance, so they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Wu Jie at Heshangyuan, they found the terrain impassable and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 伏兵起，且戰且走。

translations.literal: Ambush troops rose up; they fought as they retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Song ambushes struck; they fought a fighting retreat.

sentences.zh: 行三十裏，將至平地，宋軍陣于山口，宗弼大敗，將士多戰沒。

translations.literal: After marching thirty li, when about to reach level ground, the Song army formed battle lines at the mountain pass; Zongbi suffered a great defeat and many officers and soldiers died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty li, as they neared open ground, Song forces blocked the pass. Zongbi was routed and many of his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，複攻和尚原，克之。

translations.literal: The next year, he again attacked Heshangyuan and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked Heshangyuan again and took it.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，為右副元帥，封沈王。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, he became Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Tianhui reign, he was appointed Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 詔「諸州郡軍旅之事，決于帥府。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Military affairs of all prefectures and commanderies shall be decided by the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "All military affairs of prefectures and commanderies shall be decided by the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 民訟錢谷，行台尚書省治之」。

translations.literal: Civil lawsuits and revenue grain shall be handled by the Branch Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Civil suits and fiscal matters shall be handled by the Branch Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 宗弼兼總其事，遂議南伐。

translations.literal: Zongbi concurrently oversaw all these matters and thereupon deliberated on a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi held overall authority in both spheres and began planning a southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 太師宗幹以下皆曰：「構蒙再造之恩，不思報德，妄自鴟張，祈求無厭，今若不取，後恐難圖。」

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Zonggan and those below all said: "Gou has received the grace of being restored to life yet does not think to repay virtue; he presumptuously spreads his wings like an owl; his demands are insatiable; if we do not take action now, later it may be hard to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Zonggan and the others said: "Gou was spared and restored to his throne, yet shows no gratitude. He grows arrogant and his demands know no end. If we do not strike now, he may become impossible to subdue."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「彼將謂我不能奄有河南之地。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "They will think I cannot fully possess the lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "They will think I cannot hold all the territory south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 且都元帥久在方面，深究利害，宜即舉兵討之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Commander-in-Chief has long been in the regions and has deeply investigated advantage and harm; he should immediately raise troops to punish them."
translations.idiomatic: The Commander-in-Chief has long governed the frontier and knows its strengths and weaknesses. Let him march at once to chastise them."

sentences.zh: 遂命元帥府複河南疆土，詔中外。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the marshal's headquarters to recover the territory of Henan south of the river and issued an edict throughout the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the marshal's headquarters to recover the Henan territories and proclaimed this throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 宗弼由黎陽趨汴，右監軍撒離喝出河中趨陝西。

translations.literal: Zongbi from Liyang hurried to Bian; the Right Military Supervisor Saliehe from Hezhong hurried to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi advanced from Liyang on Bian, while the Right Military Supervisor Saliehe moved from Hezhong into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 宋岳飛、韓世忠分據河南州郡要害，複出兵涉河東，駐嵐、石、保德之境，以相牽制。

translations.literal: The Song Yue Fei and Han Shizhong separately held key prefectures and commanderies of Henan south of the river, again sent troops across east of the river, and garrisoned the regions of Lan, Shi, and Baode to restrain each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei and Han Shizhong held key points in Henan and sent forces east of the river into Lan, Shi, and Baode to tie down the Jin.

sentences.zh: 宗弼遣孔彥舟下汴、鄭兩州，王伯龍取陳州，李成取洛陽，自率眾取亳州及順昌府，嵩、汝等州相次皆下。

translations.literal: Zongbi sent Kong Yanzou down on the two prefectures Bian and Zheng, Wang Bolong to take Chenzhou, Li Cheng to take Luoyang, and himself led the host to take Bozhou and Shunchang Prefecture; Song, Ru, and other prefectures fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi sent Kong Yanzou against Bian and Zheng, Wang Bolong to take Chenzhou, and Li Cheng to take Luoyang, while he led the main force to capture Bozhou and Shunchang. Song, Ru, and other prefectures fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 時暑，宗弼還軍于汴，岳飛等軍皆退去，河南平，時天眷三年也。

translations.literal: It was hot; Zongbi returned the army to Bian; Yue Fei and other armies all withdrew; Henan south of the river was pacified—it was the third year of Tianjuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the heat of summer Zongbi withdrew to Bian. Yue Fei and the other Song armies pulled back, and Henan was pacified—in the third year of Tianjuan.

sentences.zh: 上使使勞問宗弼以下將士，凡有功軍士三千，並加忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to comfort Zongbi and the officers and soldiers below; all three thousand soldiers with merit were promoted to Loyal and Brave Company Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to reward Zongbi and his officers and men; three thousand soldiers with merit were promoted to Loyal and Brave Company Commander.

sentences.zh: 攻嵐、石、保德皆克之。

translations.literal: Attacks on Lan, Shi, and Baode all captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Lan, Shi, and Baode were all taken.

sentences.zh: 宗弼入朝，是時，上幸燕京，宗弼見於行在所。

translations.literal: Zongbi entered court; at this time the emperor was visiting Yanjing; Zongbi was received at the mobile imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi came to court while the emperor was at Yanjing and was received at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 居再旬，宗弼還軍，上起立，酌酒飲之，賜以甲胄弓矢及馬二匹。

translations.literal: After staying two ten-day periods, Zongbi returned to the army; the emperor rose, poured wine and drank with him, and bestowed armor, bow and arrows, and two horses.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days he prepared to return to the army. The emperor rose, shared a cup of wine with him, and granted armor, bow and arrows, and two horses.

sentences.zh: 宗弼已啟行四日，召還。

translations.literal: Zongbi had already set out for four days when he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Four days after he had set out, he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 至日，希尹誅。

translations.literal: On the day he arrived, Xiyin was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he arrived, Xiyin was put to death.

sentences.zh: 越五日，宗弼還軍，進伐淮南，克廬州。

translations.literal: Five days later, Zongbi returned to the army, advanced to campaign in Huainan, and captured Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later he marched again, campaigning in Huainan and capturing Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 上幸燕京，宗弼朝燕京，乞取江南，上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Yanjing; Zongbi attended court at Yanjing, begged to take the lands south of the Yangtze, and the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Yanjing, Zongbi attended court and asked permission to conquer the south; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 制詔都元帥宗弼比還軍，與宰臣同入奏事。

translations.literal: An edict was issued that Commander-in-Chief Zongbi, when he next returned from the army, should enter together with the chief ministers to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that when Commander-in-Chief Zongbi next returned from campaign he should report to the throne jointly with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 俄為尚書左丞相兼侍中，太保、都元帥、領行台如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he became Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Palace Attendant, Grand Guardian, Commander-in-Chief, and continued to head the Branch Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Palace Attendant, retaining his titles of Grand Guardian, Commander-in-Chief, and head of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔以燕京路隸尚書省，西京及山后諸部族隸元帥府。

translations.literal: An edict placed the Yanjing circuit under the Department of State Affairs and the Western Capital and the various tribes north of the mountains under the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed the Yanjing circuit under the central secretariat and the Western Capital with the tribes north of the Yan Mountains under the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 乃還軍，遂伐江南。

translations.literal: He then returned to the army and thereupon campaigned against the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the army and marched south against the Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 既渡淮，以書責讓宋人，宋人答書乞加寬宥。

translations.literal: Having crossed the Huai, he sent a letter reproaching the Song; the Song replied with a letter begging greater leniency.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Huai he sent a letter of rebuke to the Song, who replied begging for mercy.

sentences.zh: 宗弼令宋主遣信臣來稟議，宋主乞「先斂兵，許弊邑拜表闕下」，宗弼以便宜約以畫淮水為界。

translations.literal: Zongbi ordered the Song emperor to send a trusted minister to report for deliberation; the Song emperor begged "first to withdraw troops, and permit our humble state to submit a memorial at the imperial court"; Zongbi on his own authority agreed to set the Huai River as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi demanded that the Song emperor send a trusted envoy to negotiate. The emperor asked that troops be withdrawn first and that his state be allowed to submit a memorial at court. Zongbi, acting on his own authority, agreed to fix the Huai River as the border.

sentences.zh: 上遣護衛將軍撒改往軍中勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Palace Guard General Sagai to the army to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Guard General Sagai to the army to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年二月，宗弼朝京師，兼監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Huangtong, Zongbi attended court at the capital and was made Concurrent Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Huangtong, Zongbi came to the capital and was appointed concurrent supervisor of the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 宋主遣端明殿學士何鑄等進誓表，其表曰：「臣構言，今來畫疆，合以淮水中流為界，西有唐、鄧州割屬上國。

translations.literal: The Song emperor sent Academician of the Duanming Hall He Zhu and others to present a sworn memorial; the memorial said: "Your subject Gou states: Now that the boundary is to be drawn, it should take the midstream of the Huai as the border; to the west, Tang and Deng prefectures are ceded to the superior state.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor sent He Zhu of the Duanming Hall and others with a sworn memorial, which read: "Your subject Gou reports: The boundary shall run along the midstream of the Huai. Tang and Deng prefectures to the west are ceded to Your Majesty's state.

sentences.zh: 自鄧州西四十裏並南四十裏為界，屬鄧州。

translations.literal: From forty li west of Dengzhou and forty li south as the boundary, this belongs to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li west and forty li south of Dengzhou shall mark the border, remaining under Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 其四十裏外並西南盡屬光化軍，為弊邑沿邊州城。

translations.literal: Beyond forty li and all to the southwest belong to Guanghua Army, as frontier prefectures and cities of our humble state.
translations.idiomatic: All beyond forty li to the southwest shall belong to Guanghua Army as frontier posts of our humble state.

sentences.zh: 既蒙恩造，許備籓方，世世子孫，謹守臣節。

translations.literal: Having received your gracious creation and permission to serve as a frontier domain, generation after generation my descendants shall diligently observe the duties of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Having received Your Majesty's grace in permitting us to remain as a vassal domain, my descendants for generations shall faithfully observe the duties of subjects.

sentences.zh: 每年皇帝生辰並正旦，遣使稱賀不絕。

translations.literal: Each year on the emperor's birthday and at New Year's Day, envoys shall be sent to offer congratulations without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on Your Majesty's birthday and at New Year's Day, envoys shall be sent without fail to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 歲貢銀、絹二十五萬兩、匹，自壬戌年為首，每春季差人般送至泗州交納。

translations.literal: Annual tribute of silver and silk: two hundred fifty thousand taels and bolts; beginning with the renxu year, each spring persons shall be dispatched to transport it to Sizhou for delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute of two hundred fifty thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk shall begin in the renxu year and be delivered each spring to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 有渝此盟，明神是殛，墜命亡氏，踣其國家。

translations.literal: If this covenant is violated, may the bright spirits strike one dead, life fall and the clan perish, and the state be overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Should this covenant be broken, may the spirits destroy us, our lives end and our clans perish, and our state be cast down.

sentences.zh: 臣今既進誓表，伏望上國蚤降誓詔，庶使弊邑永有憑焉。」

translations.literal: Your subject has now presented this sworn memorial; I humbly hope the superior state will soon issue a sworn edict, so that our humble state may forever have something to rely upon."
translations.idiomatic: Having now submitted this sworn memorial, I humbly beg that Your Majesty's state issue a sworn edict in return, so that our humble realm may have a lasting pledge to rely upon."

sentences.zh: 宗弼進拜太傅。

translations.literal: Zongbi was promoted to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 乃遣左宣徽使劉筈使宋，以袞冕圭寶佩璲玉冊冊康王為宋帝。

translations.literal: He then sent the Left Imperial Insignia Commissioner Liu Ke as envoy to Song, with regalia of dragon robe, cap, jade scepter, treasure, pendant, jade book and register to invest the King of Kang as Song emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Left Imperial Insignia Commissioner Liu Ke to the Song with imperial regalia—the dragon robe, cap, jade scepter, seals, and investiture documents—to install the King of Kang as emperor of Song.

sentences.zh: 其冊文曰「皇帝若曰：咨爾宋康王趙構。

translations.literal: The text of investiture said: "The emperor says: Take counsel, O King of Kang of Song, Zhao Gou.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture text read: "The Emperor speaks: Hearken, O King of Kang of Song, Zhao Gou.

sentences.zh: 不吊，天降喪於爾邦，亟瀆齊盟，自貽顛覆，俾爾越在江表。

translations.literal: Heaven does not comfort; Heaven sent mourning upon your state; you repeatedly violated the allied covenant and brought downfall on yourself, causing you to drift south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven showed you no pity; calamity fell upon your realm. You repeatedly violated our covenant and brought ruin on yourself, driving you south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 用勤我師旅，蓋十有八年於茲。

translations.literal: Therefore I mobilized my armies—already eighteen years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore mobilized my armies, and now eighteen years have passed.

sentences.zh: 朕用震悼，斯民其何罪。

translations.literal: I am deeply shaken and grieved—what crime have these people committed?
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply grieved—what crime have these people committed?

sentences.zh: 今天其悔禍，誕誘爾衷，封奏狎至，願身列於籓輔。

translations.literal: Now Heaven repents the calamity and broadly guides your heart; sealed memorials arrive in succession; you wish to rank yourself among the frontier assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has now turned from calamity and opened your heart; your sealed memorials arrive one after another, and you wish to take your place among our frontier vassals.

sentences.zh: 今遣光祿大夫、左宣徽使劉筈等持節冊命爾為帝，國號宋，世服臣職，永為屏翰。

translations.literal: Now I send Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Imperial Insignia Commissioner Liu Ke and others bearing credentials to invest you as emperor, state name Song, generation after generation to perform subject duties, forever a screen and rampart.
translations.idiomatic: I now send Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Imperial Insignia Commissioner Liu Ke and others with credentials to invest you as emperor of the state of Song. Your line shall forever perform the duties of subjects and serve as a bulwark on our frontier.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼欽哉，其恭聽朕命。」

translations.literal: Alas, be reverent! Respectfully hear My command."
translations.idiomatic: Reverently heed My command."

sentences.zh: 仍詔天下。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The investiture was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 賜宗弼人口牛馬各千、駝百、羊萬，仍每歲宋國進貢內給銀、絹二千兩、匹。

translations.literal: Zongbi was granted a thousand persons, a thousand cattle and horses each, a hundred camels, and ten thousand sheep; moreover, each year from the Song tribute two thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk were allotted to him within.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi was granted a thousand households, a thousand each of cattle and horses, a hundred camels, and ten thousand sheep. Each year two thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk were set aside for him from the Song tribute.

sentences.zh: 宗弼表乞致仕，不許，優詔答之，賜以金券。

translations.literal: Zongbi memorialized begging to retire from office; this was not permitted; a gracious edict replied to him and granted him a gold warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi petitioned to retire, but the request was denied. He received a gracious edict in reply and was granted a gold warrant of privilege.

sentences.zh: 皇統七年，為太師，領三省事，都元帥、領行台尚書省事如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, he became Grand Preceptor, headed the Three Departments, and remained Commander-in-Chief and head of the Branch Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Huangtong he was appointed Grand Preceptor and placed in charge of the Three Departments, retaining his posts as Commander-in-Chief and head of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇統八年，薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Huangtong, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Huangtong.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，諡忠烈，十八年，配享太宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading, he was posthumously titled Loyal and Fierce; in the eighteenth year, he was granted paired sacrifice in Taizong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce, and in the eighteenth year he was enshrined for paired sacrifice in Emperor Taizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 子孛迭。

translations.literal: His son was Beidie.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Beidie.

sentences.zh: 子 亨

translations.literal: Son: Heng
translations.idiomatic: Son: Heng

sentences.zh: 亨，本名孛迭。

translations.literal: Heng, original name Beidie.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, whose original name was Beidie.

sentences.zh: 熙宗時，封芮王，為猛安，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the time of Xizong, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rui, made a meng'an chief, and promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rui, made a meng'an chief, and promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 天德初，加特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande, he was given the special advancement rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande reign he was promoted to Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 海陵忌太宗諸子，將謁太廟，以亨為右衛將軍，語在《太宗諸王傳》。

translations.literal: Hailing feared the sons of Taizong; when about to visit the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he made Heng Right Guard General—the account is in the Biographies of Taizong's Princes.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing feared Taizong's sons. When he was about to visit the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he appointed Heng Right Guard General—the full account appears in the Biographies of Taizong's Princes.

sentences.zh: 海陵賜良弓，亨性直，材勇絕人，喜自負，辭曰：「所賜弓，弱不可用。」

translations.literal: Hailing bestowed a fine bow; Heng's nature was upright, his talent and courage unmatched, and he liked to think highly of himself; he declined, saying: "The bow granted is too weak and cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing gave him a fine bow, Heng—frank by nature and unrivaled in strength and courage, and prone to pride—refused it, saying, "This bow is too weak to be of any use."

sentences.zh: 海陵遂忌之，出為真定尹，謂亨曰：「太宗諸子方強，多在河朔、山東，真定據其沖要，如其有變，欲倚卿為重耳。」

translations.literal: Hailing thereupon came to resent him and sent him out as prefect of Zhending, telling Heng: "Taizong's sons are still strong, mostly in Hebei and Shandong; Zhending occupies their strategic point; if there should be trouble, I wish to rely on you as my mainstay."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing took offense and sent him out as prefect of Zhending, telling him, "Taizong's sons are still powerful, mostly in Hebei and Shandong. Zhending lies at the strategic center. If trouble arises, I mean to rely on you as my mainstay."

sentences.zh: 其實忌亨也。

translations.literal: In truth he resented Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he feared Heng.

sentences.zh: 曆中京、東京留守。

translations.literal: He successively served as regent of the Central and Eastern capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as regent of the Central and Eastern capitals.

sentences.zh: 家奴梁遵告亨與衛士符公弼謀反，考驗無狀，遵坐誅。

translations.literal: His household slave Liang Zun reported that Heng and the guard Fu Gongbi plotted rebellion; investigation found no basis, and Zun was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: His household slave Liang Zun accused Heng and the guard Fu Gongbi of plotting rebellion, but investigation found no evidence and Zun was executed.

sentences.zh: 海陵益疑之。

translations.literal: Hailing grew still more suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's suspicions only deepened.

sentences.zh: 改廣甯尹，再任李老僧使伺察亨動靜，且令構其罪狀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Guangning; Li Laoseng was again appointed to spy on Heng's movements and was ordered to fabricate charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Guangning, and Li Laoseng was again assigned to watch Heng's movements and fabricate charges against him.

sentences.zh: 亨初除廣甯，諸公主宗婦往賀其母徒單氏，太祖長女兀魯曰：「孛迭雖稍下遷，勿以為嫌，國家視京府一也，況孛迭年富，何患不貴顯乎！」

translations.literal: When Heng was first appointed to Guangning, princesses and clan consorts went to congratulate his mother, the Tushi clan; Wulu, Taizu's eldest daughter, said: "Though Beidie has been slightly demoted, do not take it as an offense—the state treats capital prefectures alike; moreover Beidie is still in his prime—what worry is there that he will not rise to honor and eminence!"
translations.idiomatic: When Heng was first appointed to Guangning, princesses and imperial consorts came to congratulate his mother of the Tushi clan. Wulu, Taizu's eldest daughter, said, "Though Beidie has been demoted somewhat, do not take offense—the court treats all capital prefectures alike. Besides, Beidie is still in his prime. What reason is there to doubt that he will rise again?"

sentences.zh: 是時，兀魯與徒單斜也為室，斜也妾忽撻得幸于徒單後，忽撻詣後，告「兀魯語涉怨望，且指斥，又言孛迭當大貴」。

translations.literal: At this time Wulu and Tushi Xieye were co-wives; Xieye's concubine Hutà won favor after Tushi; Hutà went to Tushi and reported: "Wulu's words involve resentment and discontent, and even pointed criticism, and she also said Beidie will attain great honor."
translations.idiomatic: Wulu and Tushi Xieye were then co-wives. Xieye's concubine Hutà had won favor with Tushi and reported to her that Wulu's words smacked of resentment and even open criticism, and that she had said Beidie was destined for greatness.

sentences.zh: 海陵使蕭裕鞫之，左驗皆不敢言，遂殺兀魯而杖斜也，免其官，以兀魯怨望，斜也不先奏聞故也。

translations.literal: Hailing had Xiao Yu interrogate the matter; those on the left who could verify dared not speak; Wulu was then killed and Xieye flogged and removed from office, because of Wulu's resentment and because Xieye had not reported it first.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had Xiao Yu investigate. Witnesses dared not speak. Wulu was executed, Xieye was flogged and dismissed—for Wulu's disloyal words and because Xieye had failed to report them.

sentences.zh: 乃封忽撻為莘國夫人。

translations.literal: Hutà was then enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hutà was enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Xin.

sentences.zh: 久之，亨家奴六斤頗黠，給使總諸奴，老僧謂六斤曰：「爾渤海大族，不幸坐累為奴，寧不念為良乎！」

translations.literal: After some time, Heng's household slave Liujin was quite cunning and managed all the slaves; Laoseng said to Liujin: "You are of a great Bohai clan, unfortunately implicated and made a slave—do you not think of becoming free!"
translations.idiomatic: After some time, Heng's slave Liujin, a clever fellow who oversaw the other slaves, was approached by Laoseng: "You come from a great Bohai family, yet here you are enslaved through no fault of your own. Would you not rather be free?"

sentences.zh: 六斤識其意。

translations.literal: Liujin understood his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Liujin understood what he meant.

sentences.zh: 六斤嘗與亨侍妾私通，亨知之，怒曰：「必殺此奴！」

translations.literal: Liujin had once had illicit relations with Heng's concubine; Heng knew of it and angrily said: "I must kill this slave!"
translations.idiomatic: Liujin had slept with one of Heng's concubines. When Heng learned of it he raged, "I will kill that slave!"

sentences.zh: 六斤聞之懼，密與老僧謀告亨謀逆。

translations.literal: Liujin, hearing this, was afraid and secretly plotted with Laoseng to accuse Heng of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Liujin conspired secretly with Laoseng to accuse Heng of treason.

sentences.zh: 亨有良馬，將因海陵生辰進之，以謂生辰進馬者眾，不能以良馬自異，欲他日入見進之。

translations.literal: Heng had a fine horse and was about to present it on Hailing's birthday; he thought that many presented horses on birthdays and he could not distinguish himself with a fine horse, and wished to present it on another day when he entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: Heng had a fine horse he meant to present on Hailing's birthday, but thought that too many horses were given on such occasions and that a superb mount would stand out awkwardly. He decided to present it on another audience day instead.

sentences.zh: 六斤言亨笑海陵不識馬，不足進。

translations.literal: Liujin said Heng laughed that Hailing did not know horses and that it was not worth presenting.
translations.idiomatic: Liujin reported that Heng had mocked Hailing's ignorance of horses and said the gift was not worth offering.

sentences.zh: 亨之奴有自京師來者，具言徒單阿裏出虎誅死。

translations.literal: A slave of Heng's who had come from the capital fully reported that Tushi Ali Chuhu had been executed.
translations.idiomatic: A slave who had come from the capital told Heng in full that Tushi Ali Chuhu had been put to death.

sentences.zh: 亨曰：「彼有貸死誓券，安得誅之。」

translations.literal: Heng said: "He had a sworn warrant granting life in exchange for death—how could he be executed?"
translations.idiomatic: Heng said, "He held an iron-clad warrant of mercy. How could he be executed?"

sentences.zh: 奴曰：「必欲殺之，誓券安足用哉。」

translations.literal: The slave said: "If they are determined to kill him, of what use is a sworn warrant?"
translations.idiomatic: The slave replied, "If they are determined to kill a man, what good is any warrant?"

sentences.zh: 亨曰：「然則將及我矣。」

translations.literal: Heng said: "Then it will reach me next."
translations.idiomatic: Heng said, "Then my turn will come next."

sentences.zh: 六斤即以為怨望，遂誣亨欲因間刺海陵。

translations.literal: Liujin took this as resentment and thereupon falsely accused Heng of wishing to seize an opportunity to assassinate Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Liujin twisted these words into evidence of disloyalty and accused Heng of plotting to assassinate Hailing when the chance arose.

sentences.zh: 老僧即捕系亨以聞。

translations.literal: Laoseng immediately arrested and detained Heng and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Laoseng immediately arrested Heng and reported the case.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書耶律安禮、大理正忒裏等鞫之，亨言嘗論鐵券事，實無反心，而六斤亦自引伏與妾私通，亨嘗言欲殺之狀。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yelü Anli, Director of the Court of Judicial Review Teli, and others interrogated him; Heng said he had only discussed the iron warrant matter and truly had no rebellious intent, while Liujin also confessed himself to the illicit relations with the concubine and Heng's words about wishing to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yelü Anli and Director of the Court of Judicial Review Teli interrogated him. Heng said he had only spoken about the iron warrant and had no treasonous intent. Liujin confessed to the affair with the concubine and to Heng's threat to kill him.

sentences.zh: 安禮等還奏，海陵怒，複遣與老僧同鞫之。

translations.literal: Anli and the others returned to report; Hailing was angry and again sent them to interrogate together with Laoseng.
translations.idiomatic: When Anli and the others reported back, Hailing was furious and sent them to interrogate again together with Laoseng.

sentences.zh: 與其家奴並加榜掠，皆不伏。

translations.literal: Together with his household slaves they were all flogged under torture, and none confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his slaves were tortured, but none confessed.

sentences.zh: 老僧夜至亨囚所，使人蹴其陰間殺之。

translations.literal: Laoseng came at night to Heng's prison and had a man kick him in the groin and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Laoseng came to the prison at night and had a man kick Heng in the groin until he died.

sentences.zh: 亨比至死，不勝楚痛，聲達於外。

translations.literal: Heng, near death, could not bear the torture; his cries reached outside.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's screams of agony under torture could be heard outside the prison.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞亨死，佯為泣下，遣人諭其母曰：「爾子所犯法，當考掠，不意飲水致死。」

translations.literal: Hailing, hearing Heng was dead, pretended to weep and sent someone to inform his mother: "The crime your son violated should have been examined under torture; it was not expected that drinking water would cause death."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing heard that Heng was dead, he feigned tears and sent word to his mother: "Your son's offense warranted interrogation under torture. Who would have thought that drinking water would prove fatal?"

sentences.zh: 亨擊鞠為天下第一，常獨當數人。

translations.literal: Heng at cuju was ranked first under Heaven and often faced several men alone.
translations.idiomatic: In cuju Heng was reckoned the finest player in the realm and often held his own against several opponents at once.

sentences.zh: 馬無良惡，皆如意。

translations.literal: Whether horses were good or bad, all obeyed his will.
translations.idiomatic: Good horse or bad, all obeyed his will.

sentences.zh: 馬方馳，輒投杖馬前，側身附地，取杖而去。

translations.literal: While the horse was galloping, he would throw his staff before the horse, lean his body to the ground, take up the staff, and go.
translations.idiomatic: Even at full gallop he would cast his staff before the horse, drop to the ground alongside it, seize the staff, and remount.

sentences.zh: 每畋獵，持鐵連錘擊狐兔。

translations.literal: Whenever he hunted, he wielded an iron chain mace to strike foxes and hares.
translations.idiomatic: On the hunt he used an iron chain mace to bring down foxes and hares.

sentences.zh: 一日與海陵同行道中，遇群豕，亨曰：「吾能以錘殺之。」

translations.literal: One day traveling on the road with Hailing, they met a herd of boars; Heng said: "I can kill them with the mace."
translations.idiomatic: One day, traveling with Hailing, they came upon a herd of boars. Heng said, "I can kill them with my mace."

sentences.zh: 即奮錘遙擊，中其腹，穿入之。

translations.literal: He immediately swung the mace from afar, struck the belly, and pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: He hurled the mace from a distance, struck a boar in the belly, and drove it clean through.

sentences.zh: 終以勇力見忌焉。

translations.literal: In the end he was resented for his courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was his very prowess that made him feared.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年，海陵遣使殺諸宗室，於是殺亨妃徒單氏、次妃大氏及子羊蹄等三人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong, Hailing sent envoys to kill the various imperial clansmen; thereupon Heng's consort of the Tushi clan, his secondary consort of the Da clan, and his sons Yangti and others—three persons—were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenglong, Hailing sent agents to slaughter the imperial clansmen. Heng's principal consort of the Tushi clan, his secondary consort of the Da clan, and his sons including Yangti—three in all—were killed.

sentences.zh: 大定初，追複亨官爵，封韓王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, Heng's offices and titles were posthumously restored and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading reign his offices and titles were posthumously restored and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔有司改葬亨及妻子。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, an edict ordered the relevant offices to rebury Heng and his wife and sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered that Heng, his wife, and his sons be reburied with honor.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宗弼蹙宋主於海島，卒定畫淮之約。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Zongbi drove the Song emperor to a corner on a sea island and in the end fixed the covenant to draw the Huai as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Zongbi cornered the Song emperor on a coastal island and in the end secured the treaty that fixed the Huai as the border.

sentences.zh: 熙宗舉河南、陝西以與宋人，矯而正之者，宗弼也。

translations.literal: Xizong had yielded Henan and Shaanxi to the Song; the one who corrected that error was Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong had ceded Henan and Shaanxi to the Song, it was Zongbi who set matters right.

sentences.zh: 宗翰死，宗磐、宗雋、撻懶湛溺富貴，人人有自為之心，宗幹獨立，不能如之何，時無宗弼，金之國勢亦曰殆哉。

translations.literal: After Zonghan died, Zongpan, Zongjun, and Talan were steeped in wealth and honor; each man had a mind to act for himself; Zonggan stood alone and could do nothing about it; had there been no Zongbi at the time, the Jin state's power would also have been imperiled, one may say.
translations.idiomatic: After Zonghan's death, Zongpan, Zongjun, and Talan wallowed in wealth and privilege, each pursuing his own ends. Zonggan stood alone and could not restrain them. Without Zongbi, the Jin state would have been in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗有言曰：「宗翰之後，惟宗弼一人。」

translations.literal: Shizong once said: "After Zonghan, there is only Zongbi alone."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once said, "After Zonghan, there was only Zongbi."

sentences.zh: 非虛言也。

translations.literal: This was no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: That was no empty praise.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang

sentences.zh: 張邦昌，《宋史》有傳。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang has a biography in the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang has a biography in the History of Song.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，宗望軍圍汴，宋少帝請割三鎮地及輸歲幣、納質修好。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui, Zongwang's army besieged Bian; the Song young emperor begged to cede the three prefectures' territory and pay annual tribute and send hostages to restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui, Zongwang besieged Bian. The young Song emperor offered to cede the three prefectures, pay annual tribute, and send hostages to restore peace.

sentences.zh: 於是，邦昌為宋太宰，與肅王樞俱為質以來。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bangchang, as Song Grand Minister, came together with Prince Su Shu as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang, as Song Grand Minister, came with Prince Su Shu as hostages.

sentences.zh: 而少帝以書誘耶律余睹，宗翰、宗望複伐宋，執二帝以歸。

translations.literal: But the young emperor by letter enticed Yelü Yudu; Zonghan and Zongwang again campaigned against Song and brought the two emperors back as captives.
translations.idiomatic: But the young emperor sent a letter enticing Yelü Yudu to defect. Zonghan and Zongwang campaigned against Song again and brought both emperors back as captives.

sentences.zh: 劉彥宗乞複立趙氏，太宗不許。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzong begged to restore the Zhao house; Taizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzong petitioned to restore the Zhao dynasty, but Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 宋吏部尚書王時雍等請邦昌治國事，天會五年三月，立邦昌為大楚皇帝。

translations.literal: Song Minister of Personnel Wang Shiyong and others asked Bangchang to administer state affairs; in the third month of the fifth year of Tianhui, Bangchang was installed as emperor of Great Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong, Song Minister of Personnel, and others asked Bangchang to govern. In the third month of the fifth year of Tianhui he was installed as emperor of Great Chu.

sentences.zh: 初，少帝以康王構與邦昌為質，既而肅王樞易之，康王乃歸。

translations.literal: Initially the young emperor had the King of Kang Gou and Bangchang as hostages; thereafter Prince Su Shu was exchanged for them and the King of Kang returned.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the young emperor had sent the King of Kang and Bangchang as hostages. Prince Su Shu was later exchanged for them, and the King of Kang returned home.

sentences.zh: 及宗望再舉兵，少帝複使康王奉玉冊玉寶袞冕，增上太宗尊號請和。

translations.literal: When Zongwang again raised troops, the young emperor again sent the King of Kang bearing jade book, jade seal, dragon robe and cap to add a honorific title for Taizong and beg for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang marched again, the young emperor sent the King of Kang with jade seals, imperial regalia, and an enhanced honorific for Taizong to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 康王至磁州，而宗望已自魏縣渡河圍汴矣。

translations.literal: The King of Kang reached Cizhou, but Zongwang had already crossed the river from Wei County and was besieging Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Kang reached Cizhou only to learn that Zongwang had already crossed from Wei County and was besieging Bian.

sentences.zh: 及二帝出汴州，從大軍北來，而邦昌至汴，康王入於歸德。

translations.literal: When the two emperors left Bianzhou and followed the great army north, Bangchang arrived at Bian while the King of Kang entered Guide.
translations.idiomatic: When the two emperors left Bian and were marched north with the Jin army, Bangchang entered the city while the King of Kang withdrew to Guide.

sentences.zh: 邦昌勸進於歸德，康王已即位，罪以隱事殺之。

translations.literal: Bangchang urged advancement at Guide; the King of Kang had already ascended the throne and condemned him on a charge of concealed matters and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang urged him to take the throne at Guide, but the King of Kang had already been proclaimed emperor and had him executed on a charge of concealing court secrets.

sentences.zh: 邦昌死，太宗聞之，大怒，詔元帥府伐宋，宋主走揚州，事具宗翰等傳。

translations.literal: When Bangchang died, Taizong heard of it and was greatly enraged; he ordered the marshal's headquarters to campaign against Song; the Song emperor fled to Yangzhou—the account is in the biographies of Zonghan and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong learned of Bangchang's death he was furious and ordered the marshal's headquarters to campaign against Song. The Song emperor fled to Yangzhou—the full account appears in the biographies of Zonghan and others.

sentences.zh: 其後，太宗複立劉豫繼邦昌，號大齊。

translations.literal: Thereafter Taizong again installed Liu Yu to succeed Bangchang, titled Great Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then installed Liu Yu to succeed Bangchang as ruler of Great Qi.

sentences.zh: 劉豫，字彥游，景州阜城人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, style name Yanyou, was a native of Fucheng in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, style name Yanyou, was from Fucheng in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋宣和末，仕為河北西路提刑。

translations.literal: At the end of Song Xuanhe, he served as judicial intendant of Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe reign he served as judicial intendant of Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 徙浙西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 抵儀真，喪妻翟氏，繼值父憂。

translations.literal: Reaching Yizhen, he mourned his wife of the Zhai clan and then suffered his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yizhen, he mourned the death of his wife of the Zhai clan and then his father.

sentences.zh: 康王至揚州，樞密使張愨薦知濟南府。

translations.literal: When the King of Kang reached Yangzhou, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Zhang Que recommended him to govern Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Kang reached Yangzhou, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Que recommended him as prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東盜賊滿野，豫欲得江南一郡，宰相不與，忿忿而去。

translations.literal: At this time bandits filled the fields of Shandong; Yu wished to obtain a prefecture in the south and the chief minister would not grant it; resentful, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits then filled Shandong. Yu wanted a post south of the Yangtze, but the chief minister refused. He left in resentment.

sentences.zh: 撻懶攻濟南，有關勝者，濟南驍將也，屢出城拒戰，豫遂殺關勝出降。

translations.literal: Talan attacked Jinan; there was Guan Sheng, a fierce general of Jinan, who repeatedly sallied to resist; Yu thereupon killed Guan Sheng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Talan attacked Jinan, the city's fierce general Guan Sheng repeatedly sallied to resist. Yu killed Guan Sheng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂為京東東、西、淮南安撫使，知東平府兼諸路馬步軍都總管，節制河外諸軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon became pacification commissioner of eastern and western Jingdong and Huainan, governed Dongping Prefecture and concurrently served as overall commander of cavalry and infantry of all circuits, controlling all armies beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacification commissioner of eastern and western Jingdong and Huainan, prefect of Dongping, and overall commander of cavalry and infantry with authority over all armies beyond the river.

sentences.zh: 以豫子麟知濟南府。

translations.literal: Yu's son Lin was made prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin was appointed prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 撻懶屯兵沖要，以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Talan garrisoned troops at strategic points to pacify and control the region.
translations.idiomatic: Talan garrisoned key points to keep the region under control.

sentences.zh: 初，康王既殺張邦昌，自歸德奔揚州，詔左右副元帥合兵討之，詔曰：「俟宋平，當援立籓輔，以鎮南服，如張邦昌者。」

translations.literal: Initially, after the King of Kang had killed Zhang Bangchang and fled from Guide to Yangzhou, an edict ordered the Left and Right Deputy Commanders-in-Chief to combine forces to chastise him, stating: "When Song is pacified, a frontier assistant shall be installed to secure the southern domains, like Zhang Bangchang."
translations.idiomatic: After the King of Kang killed Zhang Bangchang and fled from Guide to Yangzhou, an edict ordered the deputy commanders-in-chief to combine forces against him, declaring, "When Song is pacified, a frontier vassal shall be installed to hold the south, as with Zhang Bangchang."

sentences.zh: 及宋主自明州入海亡去，宗弼北還，乃議更立其人。

translations.literal: When the Song emperor fled into the sea from Mingzhou, Zongbi returned north, and they deliberated on installing another person.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song emperor escaped by sea from Mingzhou and Zongbi withdrew north, the Jin debated installing another ruler.

sentences.zh: 眾議折可求、劉豫皆可立，而豫亦有心。

translations.literal: In collective deliberation Zhe Keqiu and Liu Yu were both considered installable, and Yu also had the mind for it.
translations.idiomatic: The council considered both Zhe Keqiu and Liu Yu suitable candidates, and Yu was eager for the post.

sentences.zh: 撻懶為豫求封，太宗用封張邦昌故事，以九月朔旦授策。

translations.literal: Talan sought enfeoffment for Yu; Taizong followed the precedent of enfeoffing Zhang Bangchang and granted the investiture document on the first day of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Talan pressed for Yu's installation. Taizong followed the precedent used for Zhang Bangchang and granted investiture on the first day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 受策之後，以籓王禮見使者。

translations.literal: After receiving the investiture document, he met the envoy with the rites of a frontier prince.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving investiture he received the envoy with the rites due a vassal prince.

sentences.zh: 臣宗翰、臣宗輔議：「既策為籓輔，稱臣奉表，朝廷報諭詔命，避正位與使人抗禮，餘禮並從帝者。」

translations.literal: Your subjects Zonghan and Zongfu deliberated: "Having been invested as frontier assistant, he shall style himself subject and submit memorials; the court replies with edicts of instruction; he avoids the principal seat and meets envoys with equal rites; other rites all follow those of an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects Zonghan and Zongfu proposed: "As a frontier vassal he shall style himself a subject and submit memorials, while the court replies with edicts. He shall yield the principal seat and meet envoys as an equal in rank, but otherwise observe imperial ceremonial."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今立豫為子皇帝，既為鄰國之君，又為大朝之子，其見大朝使介，惟使者始見躬問起居與面辭有奏則立，其餘並行皇帝禮。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Now Yu is installed as Son Emperor; being both ruler of a neighboring state and son of the great court, when he receives envoys of the great court, only at the envoy's first audience, personal inquiry after health, and face-to-face farewell with a memorial does he stand; for the rest he performs all imperial rites."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Yu is installed as Son Emperor—ruler of a neighboring state and son of our court. When he receives our envoys he shall stand only at their first audience, when they inquire after his health, and when they take leave with a final memorial. On all other occasions he shall observe full imperial ceremonial."

sentences.zh: 元帥府使蕭慶如汴，與豫議以伐宋事，豫報曰：「宋主軍帥韓世忠屯潤州，劉光世屯江寧。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters envoy Xiao Qing went to Bian and deliberated with Yu on campaigning against Song; Yu replied: "The Song emperor's commanders Han Shizhong are garrisoned at Runzhou and Liu Guangshi at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal's headquarters envoy Xiao Qing went to Bian to discuss a campaign against Song. Yu replied, "The Song commanders Han Shizhong are at Runzhou and Liu Guangshi at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 今舉大兵，欲往採石渡江，而劉光世拒守江寧。

translations.literal: If we now raise a great army intending to cross the river at Caishi, Liu Guangshi will hold and defend Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: If the main army crosses at Caishi, Liu Guangshi will hold Jiangning and block the route.

sentences.zh: 若出宿州抵揚州，則世忠必聚海船截瓜洲渡。

translations.literal: If we go out from Suzhou to reach Yangzhou, Shizhong will surely gather sea vessels to block the Guazhou crossing.
translations.idiomatic: If the army marches from Suzhou toward Yangzhou, Shizhong will mass his fleet to block the crossing at Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 若輕兵直趨採石，彼未有備，我必徑渡江矣。

translations.literal: If light troops hurry straight to Caishi, they will not be prepared and we will surely cross the river directly.
translations.idiomatic: But if light troops strike straight for Caishi, the Song will be unprepared and we can cross the river at once.

sentences.zh: 光世海船亦在潤州，韓世忠必先取之，二將由此必不和。

translations.literal: Guangshi's sea vessels are also at Runzhou; Han Shizhong will surely seize them first; the two generals will thereby certainly not be in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi's ships are also at Runzhou, and Shizhong will seize them first. The two generals will fall out—and that will corner the Song emperor.

sentences.zh: 以此逼宋主，其可以也。」

translations.literal: Using this to press the Song emperor—it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: That is how we can corner the Song emperor."

sentences.zh: 未幾，宋主閣門宣贊舍人徐文將大小船六十只、軍兵七百餘人來奔，至密州界中，率將佐至汴。

translations.literal: Before long, the Song emperor's Gate Guard Announcer Attendant Xu Wen brought sixty large and small vessels and more than seven hundred soldiers to defect; reaching the border of Mizhou, he led his officers to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the Song Gate Guard Announcer Xu Wen defected with sixty vessels and more than seven hundred troops. Reaching the Mizhou border, he led his officers to Bian.

sentences.zh: 豫與元帥府書曰：「徐文一行，久在海中，盡知江南利害。

translations.literal: Yu wrote to the marshal's headquarters: "Xu Wen's party has long been at sea and fully knows the advantages and harms of the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Yu wrote to the marshal's headquarters: "Xu Wen and his men have long been at sea and know the Yangtze region inside out.

sentences.zh: 文言：宋主在杭州，其候潮門外錢塘江內有船二百隻。

translations.literal: Wen said: "The Song emperor is at Hangzhou; within the Qiantang River outside the Tide-Watching Gate there are two hundred vessels."
translations.idiomatic: Wen reports that the Song emperor is at Hangzhou, with two hundred ships in the Qiantang River outside the Tide-Watching Gate.

sentences.zh: 宋主初走入海時，於此上船，過錢塘江別有河入越州，向明州定海口迤邐前去昌國縣。

translations.literal: When the Song emperor first fled into the sea, he boarded here; crossing the Qiantang River there is another river entering Yuezhou; toward Mingzhou from Dinghai mouth winding on to Changguo County.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first fled to sea he embarked here. Beyond the Qiantang there is another waterway into Yuezhou, and from Mingzhou's Dinghai harbor the route winds on to Changguo County.

sentences.zh: 其縣在海中，宋人聚船積糧之處。

translations.literal: That county is in the sea, a place where the Song gathered vessels and stockpiled grain.
translations.idiomatic: That county lies offshore—the place where the Song stockpile ships and grain.

sentences.zh: 今大軍可先往昌國縣，攻取船糧，還趨明州城下，奪取宋主禦船，直抵錢塘江口。

translations.literal: Now the great army can first go to Changguo County, seize ships and grain, then turn back and hurry to below Mingzhou city, seize the Song emperor's imperial vessels, and reach straight to the mouth of the Qiantang River.
translations.idiomatic: The main army should strike Changguo County first, seize its ships and supplies, then swing back to Mingzhou, capture the emperor's fleet, and push straight to the mouth of the Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 今自密州上船，如風勢順，可五日夜到昌國縣，或風勢稍慢，十日或半月可至。」

translations.literal: If boarding at Mizhou now, with favorable winds it can reach Changguo County in five days and nights, or if the wind is somewhat slow, ten days or half a month can suffice to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Embarking from Mizhou, with fair winds the voyage takes five days; with slower winds, ten days to half a month."

sentences.zh: 初，宗弼自江南北還，宗翰將入朝，再議以伐宋事。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Zongbi returned from south of the Yangtze; Zonghan was about to enter court and again deliberated on campaigning against Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Zongbi returned from south of the Yangtze. As Zonghan prepared to attend court, the court debated invading Song once more.

sentences.zh: 宗翰堅執以為可伐。

translations.literal: Zonghan firmly maintained that Song could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan insisted that Song could be attacked.

sentences.zh: 宗弼曰：「江南卑濕，今士馬困憊，糧儲未豐足，恐無成功。」

translations.literal: Zongbi said: "The lands south of the Yangtze are low and damp; now soldiers and horses are weary and exhausted, grain stores are not yet plentiful and sufficient—I fear there will be no success."
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi objected: "The south is low and damp. Our troops and horses are exhausted and supplies are still short. I doubt we can succeed."

sentences.zh: 宗翰曰：「都監務偷安爾。」

translations.literal: Zonghan said: "The Marshal Supervisor only seeks ease and comfort, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan retorted: "The Marshal Supervisor only wants an easy life."

sentences.zh: 及豫以書報，而睿宗亦不肯用豫策，使撻懶帥師至瓜洲而還。

translations.literal: When Yu reported by letter, Ruizong also would not adopt Yu's plan and sent Talan to command troops to Guazhou and back.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu's report arrived, Ruizong likewise rejected his plan and sent Talan to lead troops to Guazhou, then recalled them.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，制詔「齊國與本朝軍民相訴，關涉文移，署年止用天會」。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui, an ordinance edicted: "When the Qi state and this court's military and civilians sue each other, documents involved in the matter shall for dating use only Tianhui."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 14 an edict ruled that legal disputes between the Qi regime and the Jin court, and all related documents, were to be dated only by the Tianhui reign era.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，詔廢齊國，降封豫為蜀王。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, an edict abolished the Qi state and demoted Yu, enfeoffing him as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15 an edict abolished the Qi state and demoted Liu Yu to King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 豫稱大號凡八年。

translations.literal: Yu had claimed the great title for altogether eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had borne the imperial title for eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 於是，置行台尚書省於汴，除去豫弊政，人情大悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Branch Secretariat was established at Bian, Yu's bad policies were removed, and popular sentiment was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The court then established a Branch Secretariat at Bian, abolished Yu's abusive policies, and won broad popular approval.

sentences.zh: 以故齊宰相張孝純權行台左丞相，遂遷豫家屬于臨潢府。

translations.literal: The former Qi chancellor Zhang Xiaochun was appointed provisional Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, and Yu's household was then moved to Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qi chancellor Zhang Xiaochun was named acting Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, and Yu's family was relocated to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 麟字元瑞，豫之子也。

translations.literal: Lin, style name Yuanrui, was Yu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, courtesy name Yuanrui, was Liu Yu's son.

sentences.zh: 宋宣和間，父廕補將仕郎，累加承務郎。

translations.literal: During Song's Xuanhe reign, by his father's privilege he was appointed Replenishment Gentleman for Attendance and successively promoted to Gentleman for Court Service.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe era he entered office by his father's privilege as a Replenishment Gentleman and rose to Gentleman for Court Service.

sentences.zh: 天會七年，豫以濟南降，麟因從軍，討水賊王江，破降之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui, when Yu surrendered Jinan, Lin followed the army, campaigned against the river bandit Wang Jiang, defeated and accepted his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 7, when Yu surrendered Jinan, Lin joined the army, defeated the river bandit Wang Jiang, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 豫節制東平，以麟知濟南府事。

translations.literal: Yu oversaw Dongping and appointed Lin to know the affairs of Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner for Dongping, Yu put Lin in charge of Jinan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，以濟南為興平軍，麟為節度使、開府儀同三司、梁國公，充諸路兵馬大總管，判濟南府事。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, Jinan was made Xingping Army; Lin became military commissioner, Pillar of the State with Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, Duke of Liang, filling the Grand Commander of Military and Horse of all circuits, and disposing Jinan Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was founded, Jinan became Xingping Army command. Lin was made military commissioner, honored with the rank of Pillar of State with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, appointed grand commander of all circuit forces, and given charge of Jinan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，為齊尚書左丞相。

translations.literal: The next year he became Qi's Left Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Qi state's Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 明年，從豫遷汴，罷判濟南，依前開府，聽置參謀。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Yu in moving to Bian, was dismissed from disposing Jinan, continued as before with an open prefecture, and was permitted to appoint staff advisers.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he accompanied Yu to Bian. He relinquished his post at Jinan but kept his honorary open prefecture and was allowed advisers on staff.

sentences.zh: 豫請立麟為太子，朝廷不許，曰：「若與我伐宋有功則立之。」

translations.literal: Yu requested to install Lin as heir apparent; the court did not approve and said: "If he has achievement in campaigning against Song for us, then he may be installed."
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked to name Lin crown prince. The court refused: "Only if he earns merit campaigning against Song for us will we consider it."

sentences.zh: 於是，麟連歲帥兵南伐，皆無功而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lin for successive years commanded troops in southern campaigns, all without achievement and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Lin then led southern campaigns year after year, each ending in failure.

sentences.zh: 昌，本名撻懶，穆宗子。

translations.literal: Chang, original name Talan, was a son of Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose original name was Talan, was a son of Muzong.

sentences.zh: 宗翰襲遼主於鴛鴦濼，遼都統馬哥奔搗裏，撻懶收其群牧。

translations.literal: Zonghan attacked the Liao ruler at Yuanyang Marsh; the Liao supreme commander Mage fled to Daoli; Talan collected his herd flocks.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan struck the Liao emperor at Yuanyang Marsh, Liao supreme commander Mage fled to Daoli; Talan seized his herds.

sentences.zh: 宗翰使撻懶追擊之，不及，獲遼樞密使得裏底及其子磨哥、那野以還。

translations.literal: Zonghan sent Talan to pursue him but could not overtake; he captured the Liao Privy Council director Delidi and his sons Moge and Naye and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan sent Talan in pursuit but could not catch Mage. Talan did capture the Liao Privy Council director Delidi and his sons Moge and Naye.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將襲遼主於大魚濼，留輜重於草濼，使撻懶、牙卯守之。

translations.literal: Taizu personally led troops to attack the Liao ruler at Dayu Marsh, left baggage at Cao Marsh, and ordered Talan and Yamou to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu personally attacked the Liao emperor at Dayu Marsh, leaving the baggage train at Cao Marsh under Talan and Yamou.

sentences.zh: 奚路兵官渾黜不能安輯其眾，遂以撻懶為奚六路軍帥鎮之。

translations.literal: The Xilu military officer Hun Chu could not settle and bring together his multitude, so Talan was made commander of the Six Xilu Armies to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xilu officer Hun Chu failed to control his troops, Talan was made commander of the Six Xilu Armies to restore order.

sentences.zh: 習古乃、婆盧火護送常勝軍及燕京豪族工匠自松亭關入內地，上戒之曰：「若遇險厄，則分兵以往。」

translations.literal: Xigunai and Baluhuo escorted the Ever-Victorious Army and Yanjing noble clans' craftsmen through Songting Pass into the interior; the emperor warned them: "If you encounter peril and hardship, then divide the troops to proceed."
translations.idiomatic: Xigunai and Baluhuo escorted the Ever-Victorious Army and Yanjing nobles and craftsmen through Songting Pass. The emperor instructed them: "If the route grows dangerous, split your forces."

sentences.zh: 習古乃、婆盧火乃合於撻懶。

translations.literal: Xigunai and Baluhuo then joined with Talan.
translations.idiomatic: Xigunai and Baluhuo then joined Talan's command.

sentences.zh: 久之，討劾山速古部奚人。

translations.literal: After a long time he campaigned against the Xi people of the Kesunshan Sugubu.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he campaigned against the Xi of the Kesunshan Sugubu.

sentences.zh: 奚人據險戰，殺且盡，速古、啜裏、鐵尼十三砦皆平之。

translations.literal: The Xi held strategic terrain and fought; they were nearly all killed; Sugu, Chueli, Tieni, and thirteen stockades were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi fought from strong positions and were nearly annihilated. Thirteen stockades—including Sugu, Chueli, and Tieni—were pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕以奚路險阻，經略為難，命汝往任其事，而克副所托，良用嘉歎。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We, because the Xilu route is rugged and obstructed and its management difficult, ordered you to go and take on this matter, and you have fulfilled what was entrusted—truly worthy of praise and sighs of approval.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The Xilu country is rugged and hard to govern. I sent you to take charge, and you have fully met my expectations. I commend you warmly.

sentences.zh: 今回離保部族來附，餘眾奔潰，無能為已。

translations.literal: Now the Huilibao tribes have come to attach themselves; the remaining multitude flees in rout and can do nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The Huilibao tribes have now submitted; the rest have scattered and can do no more harm.

sentences.zh: 比命習古乃、波盧火獲送降人，若遇險阻，即分兵以行，餘眾悉與汝合。

translations.literal: Recently Xigunai and Boluhuo were ordered to escort surrendered people; if they encounter rugged obstacles, then divide troops to proceed; the remaining multitude shall all join you.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered Xigunai and Boluhuo to escort surrendered peoples. If they meet difficult terrain they are to divide their forces; the remainder will join your command.

sentences.zh: 降詔二十，招諭未降，汝當審度其事，從宜處之。」

translations.literal: Twenty surrender edicts are issued to summon and instruct those not yet surrendered; you should carefully assess the matter and handle it as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: Twenty edicts of surrender have been issued to win over those still holding out. Assess each case and act as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 其後撫定奚部及分南路邊界，表請設官鎮守。
