translations.literal: Afterward he pacified and settled the Xi tribes and divided the southern-route frontier, memorializing to request establishing officials to garrison and guard.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the Xi tribes, delineated the southern frontier, and memorialized for garrison officials.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「依東京渤海列置千戶、謀克。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Follow the precedent of Eastern Capital and Bohai in establishing offices of thousand-households and company-commanders."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered: "Follow the Eastern Capital and Bohai precedent—establish thousand-household and company-commander offices."

sentences.zh: 遼外戚遙輦昭古牙部族在建州，斜野襲走之，獲其妻孥及官豪之族。

translations.literal: The Liao maternal-clan Yaolian Zhaoguya tribe in Jianzhou was raided and driven off by Xieye, who captured their wives, children, and the families of officials and magnates.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye raided the Liao maternal-clan Yaolian Zhaoguya tribe at Jianzhou, driving them off and capturing their women, children, and leading families.

sentences.zh: 撻懶複擊之，擒其隊將曷魯燥、白撒葛，殺之，降民戶千餘，進降金源縣。

translations.literal: Talan again attacked them, captured their squad commanders Heluzao and Basage, killed them, accepted surrender of more than a thousand households, and advanced to pacify Jinyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Talan struck again, captured squad commanders Heluzao and Basage and killed them, accepted the surrender of more than a thousand households, and advanced to pacify Jinyuan County.

sentences.zh: 詔增賜銀牌十。

translations.literal: An edict increased his gift by ten silver plaques.
translations.idiomatic: He was awarded ten additional silver plaques.

sentences.zh: 又降遙輦二部，再破興中兵，降建州官屬，得山砦二十，村堡五百八十。

translations.literal: He again subdued two Yaolian divisions, twice defeated Xingzhong troops, accepted surrender of Jianzhou official retainers, obtained twenty mountain stockades and five hundred eighty village forts.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued two more Yaolian divisions, twice defeated Xingzhong forces, accepted the surrender of Jianzhou officials, and took twenty mountain stockades and five hundred eighty villages.

sentences.zh: 阿忽複敗昭古牙，降其官民尤多。

translations.literal: Ahu again defeated Zhaoguya and accepted surrender of still more of his officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Ahu defeated Zhaoguya again and brought over an even larger body of officials and people.

sentences.zh: 昭古牙勢蹙亦降，興中、建州皆平。

translations.literal: Zhaoguya, pressed hard, also surrendered; Xingzhong and Jianzhou were both pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoguya, cornered, surrendered as well. Xingzhong and Jianzhou were pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔第將士功賞，撫安新民。

translations.literal: An edict ranked officers' and soldiers' merits for reward, and pacified and settled the newly submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were apportioned by merit, and the newly submitted populace was settled.

sentences.zh: 撻懶請以遙輦九營為九猛安。

translations.literal: Talan requested to make the nine Yaolian camps into nine meng'an districts.
translations.idiomatic: Talan asked to organize the nine Yaolian camps into nine meng'an districts.

sentences.zh: 上以奪鄰有功，使領四猛安，昭古牙仍為親管猛安。

translations.literal: The emperor, because seizing neighboring territory had merit, had him lead four meng'an; Zhaoguya remained a personally administered meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in seizing neighboring territory the emperor gave him four meng'an to command. Zhaoguya remained a personally supervised meng'an.

sentences.zh: 五猛安之都帥，命撻懶擇人授之。

translations.literal: For the five meng'an commanders-in-chief, Talan was ordered to choose men and appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: Talan was told to choose and appoint commanders for the other five meng'an.

sentences.zh: 撻懶與劉彥宗舉蕭公翊為興中尹，郡府各以契丹、漢官攝治，上皆從之。

translations.literal: Talan with Liu Yanzong recommended Xiao Gongyi as Xingzhong governor; each prefecture and magistracy was to be administered in proxy by Khitan and Han officials—the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: Talan and Liu Yanzong recommended Xiao Gongyi as governor of Xingzhong; county and prefectural offices were filled with Khitan and Han officials in acting posts, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 及宗翰、宗望伐宋，撻懶為六部路都統。

translations.literal: When Zonghan and Zongwang campaigned against Song, Talan was supreme commander of the Six-Bu Route.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan and Zongwang invaded Song, Talan served as supreme commander of the Six-Bu Route.

sentences.zh: 宗望已受宋盟，軍還，撻懶乃歸中京。

translations.literal: Zongwang had already accepted Song's alliance and the army returned; Talan then returned to Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongwang accepted the Song alliance and withdrew, Talan returned to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 天會四年八月，複伐宋。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Tianhui, Song was again attacked.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianhui 4 the Jin invaded Song again.

sentences.zh: 閏月，宗翰、宗望軍皆至汴州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, the armies of Zonghan and Zongwang both reached Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month the forces of Zonghan and Zongwang reached Bian.

sentences.zh: 撻懶、阿裏刮破宋兵二萬於杞，覆其三營，獲京東路都總管胡直孺及其二子與南路都統制隋師元及其三將，遂克拱州，降寧陵，破睢陽，下亳州。

translations.literal: Talan and Aligua defeated twenty thousand Song troops at Qi, overthrew their three camps, captured Eastern Capital Circuit Grand Commander Hu Zhiru and his two sons and Southern Circuit Commander-in-Chief Sui Shiyuan and his three generals, then took Gongzhou, accepted Ningling's surrender, broke Suixiang, and subdued Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi, Talan and Aligua routed twenty thousand Song troops, destroyed three camps, and captured Eastern Circuit grand commander Hu Zhiru with his two sons, southern circuit commander Sui Shiyuan, and three of his generals. They took Gongzhou, received the surrender of Ningling, stormed Suixiang, and seized Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋兵來複睢陽，又擊走之，擒其將石瑱。

translations.literal: Song troops came to retake Suixiang; he again attacked and drove them off, capturing their general Shi Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces tried to retake Suixiang he drove them off again and captured general Shi Zhen.

sentences.zh: 宋二帝已降，大軍北還，撻懶為元帥左監軍，徇地山東，取密州。

translations.literal: The two Song emperors had already surrendered; the great army returned north; Talan was Left Supervisor of the Marshal and mopped up Shandong, taking Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the two Song emperors surrendered and the main army withdrew north, Talan became Left Supervisor of the Marshal, secured Shandong, and took Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 迪虎取單州，撻懶取巨鹿，阿裏刮取宗城，迪古不取清平、臨清，蒙刮取趙州，阿裏刮徇下浚、滑、恩及高唐，分遣諸將趣磁、信德，皆降之。

translations.literal: Dihu took Danzhou; Talan took Julu; Aligua took Zongcheng; Digubu took Qingping and Linqing; Menggua took Zhaozhou; Aligua swept Xia, Hua, En, and Gaotang; dispatching various generals toward Ci and Xinde, all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Dihu took Danzhou; Talan Julu; Aligua Zongcheng; Digubu Qingping and Linqing; Menggua Zhaozhou. Aligua swept through Xia, Hua, En, and Gaotang while detachments advanced on Ci and Xinde—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 劉豫以濟南府降，詔以豫為安撫使，治東平，撻懶以左監軍鎮撫之，大事專決焉。

translations.literal: Liu Yu surrendered by Jinan Prefecture; an edict made Yu Pacification Commissioner, governing Dongping; Talan as Left Supervisor pacified and controlled the region, with major affairs exclusively decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu surrendered Jinan, he was made Pacification Commissioner with his seat at Dongping. Talan, as Left Supervisor, governed the region and held final authority on major affairs.

sentences.zh: 後為右副元帥。

translations.literal: Later he became Right Deputy Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Right Deputy Marshal.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年為左副元帥，封魯國王。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he became Left Deputy Marshal and was enfeoffed King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15 he became Left Deputy Marshal and was enfeoffed as King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 初，宋人既誅張邦昌，太宗詔諸將複求如邦昌者立之，或舉折可求，撻懶力舉劉豫。

translations.literal: At the beginning, after the Song had executed Zhang Bangchang, Taizong ordered the generals again to seek one like Bangchang to install; some recommended Zhe Keqiu; Talan forcefully recommended Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song executed Zhang Bangchang, Taizong ordered his generals to find another puppet ruler like him. Some favored Zhe Keqiu, but Talan strongly backed Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 豫立為帝，號大齊。

translations.literal: Yu was installed as emperor, styled Great Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was enthroned as emperor of Great Qi.

sentences.zh: 豫為帝數年，無尺寸功，遂廢豫為蜀王。

translations.literal: Yu reigned as emperor several years without the slightest achievement, and was then deposed, enfeoffed as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After several years as emperor without earning the slightest merit, Yu was deposed and made King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 撻懶與右副元帥宗弼俱在河南，宋使王倫求河南、陝西地於撻懶。

translations.literal: Talan and Right Deputy Marshal Zongbi were both in Henan; the Song envoy Wang Lun sought Henan and Shaanxi territory from Talan.
translations.idiomatic: Talan and Right Deputy Marshal Zongbi were both in Henan when the Song envoy Wang Lun asked Talan to cede Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，撻懶朝京師，倡議以廢齊舊地與宋，熙宗命群臣議，會東京留守宗雋來朝，與撻懶合力，宗幹等爭之不能得。

translations.literal: The next year Talan attended court at the capital, initiating the proposal to give the abolished Qi's old territory to Song; Xizong ordered the ministers to deliberate; it happened that Eastern Capital garrison commander Zongjun came to court and united strength with Talan; Zonggan and others contended but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Talan went to court and proposed ceding the former Qi territories to Song. Xizong ordered a debate. Eastern Capital commander Zongjun arrived and joined him. Zonggan and others objected but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 宗雋曰：「我以地與宋，宋必德我。」

translations.literal: Zongjun said: "If we give territory to Song, Song will surely be grateful to us."
translations.idiomatic: Zongjun argued: "If we give the land to Song, they will be grateful to us."

sentences.zh: 宗憲折之日：「我俘宋人父兄，怨非一日。

translations.literal: Zongxian refuted him, saying: "We captured the Song people's fathers and elder brothers—their resentment is not of a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxian objected: "We hold their emperors and fathers captive. Their hatred is deep and long-standing.

sentences.zh: 若複資以土地，是助仇也，何德之有。

translations.literal: If we again supply them with territory, that is aiding the enemy—what gratitude would there be.
translations.idiomatic: Giving them land now only strengthens an enemy. Where is the gratitude in that?

sentences.zh: 勿與便。」

translations.literal: Do not give it—so be it."
translations.idiomatic: Do not cede the territory."

sentences.zh: 撻懶弟勖亦以為不可。

translations.literal: Talan's younger brother Xu also held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Talan's brother Xu also opposed the cession.

sentences.zh: 既退，撻懶責勖曰：「他人尚有從我者，汝乃異議乎。」

translations.literal: After they withdrew, Talan reproached Xu: "Others still have some who follow me—yet you raise a separate opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: After the session Talan rebuked Xu: "Others side with me—must you dissent?"

sentences.zh: 勖曰：「苟利國家，豈敢私邪。」

translations.literal: Xu said: "If it profits the state, how would I dare privy partiality."
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied: "If it serves the state, I will not put private loyalty above public good."

sentences.zh: 是時，太宗長子宗磐為宰相，位在宗幹上，撻懶、宗雋附之，竟執議以河南、陝西地與宋。

translations.literal: At this time Taizong's eldest son Zongpan was chancellor, ranking above Zonggan; Talan and Zongjun attached to him and ultimately carried the deliberation to give Henan and Shaanxi territory to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's eldest son Zongpan was chancellor, outranking Zonggan. Talan and Zongjun backed him, and the court voted to cede Henan and Shaanxi to Song.

sentences.zh: 張通古為詔諭江南使。

translations.literal: Zhang Tonggu was made envoy to instruct and announce to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tonggu was sent as envoy to announce the settlement to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 久子，宗磐跋扈尤甚，宗雋亦為丞相，撻懶持兵柄，謀反有狀。

translations.literal: After a long time, Zongpan's overbearing violence was extreme; Zongjun also became chancellor; Talan held military authority—there were signs of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In time Zongpan grew defiant, Zongjun became chancellor, and Talan held the armies—clear signs of a conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 宗磐、宗雋皆伏誅，詔以撻懶屬尊，有大功，因釋不問，出為行台尚書左丞相，手詔慰遣。

translations.literal: Zongpan and Zongjun were both executed; an edict said that because Talan was of the imperial clan and had great achievement, he was therefore released without inquiry, sent out as Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, with a handwritten edict comforting and dismissing him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongpan and Zongjun were executed. Talan was kin to the imperial line and had rendered great service, so he was spared, demoted to Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, and sent away with a personal edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 撻懶至燕京，愈驕肆不法，複與翼王鶻懶謀反，而朝議漸知其初與宋交通而倡議割河南、陝西之地。

translations.literal: Talan reached Yanjing and grew ever more arrogant, unrestrained, and lawless; again conspired rebellion with Prince of Yi Helan; and court discussion gradually knew that at first he had communicated with Song and initiated the proposal to cede Henan and Shaanxi territory.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanjing Talan grew still more lawless and plotted again with Prince of Yi Helan. The court gradually realized he had colluded with Song when he first proposed ceding Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 宗弼請複取河南、陝西。

translations.literal: Zongbi requested to retake Henan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi urged retaking Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 會有上變告撻懶者，熙宗乃下詔誅之。

translations.literal: It happened that someone presented a petition reporting Talan's rebellion; Xizong then issued an edict to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When a petition accused Talan of treason, Xizong ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 撻懶自燕京南走，追而殺之于祁州，並殺翼王及宗人活離胡土、撻懶二子斡帶、烏達補，而赦其黨與。

translations.literal: Talan fled south from Yanjing; pursued and killed at Qizhou; the Prince of Yi and clansmen Holi Hutu were also killed; Talan's two sons Wodai and Wudabu were killed; his faction and associates were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Talan fled south from Yanjing and was overtaken and killed at Qizhou. The Prince of Yi and kinsmen Holi Hutu were killed with him, as were Talan's sons Wodai and Wudabu. His associates were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 宗弼為都元帥，再定河南、陝西。

translations.literal: Zongbi became supreme marshal and again secured Henan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi became supreme marshal and reconquered Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 伐宋渡淮，宋康王乞和，遂稱臣，畫淮為界，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Song he crossed the Huai; the Song Prince of Kang begged peace, then declared himself subject; the Huai was drawn as the boundary, and troops were then halted.
translations.idiomatic: Invading Song he crossed the Huai. The Prince of Kang (Gaozong) sued for peace, submitted as a vassal, and accepted the Huai as the boundary—then the armies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君臣之位，如冠屨定分，不可頃刻易也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The positions of ruler and minister are like hat and shoes in fixed rank—they cannot be changed for even a moment.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Ruler and subject occupy fixed ranks, like hat above shoes—they must not be reversed even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 五季亂極，綱常斁壞。

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties' chaos reached its extreme; constant principles were destroyed and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties brought chaos to its peak and shattered the moral order.

sentences.zh: 遼之太宗，慢褻神器，倒置冠屨，援立石晉，以臣易君，宇宙以來之一大變也。

translations.literal: Liao's Taizong contemptuously profaned the sacred vessel, inverted hat and shoes, supported and installed the Later Jin of Shi Jingtang, exchanging subject for ruler—a great transformation since the cosmos began.
translations.idiomatic: Liao's Emperor Taizong profaned the imperial mandate, reversed the natural order, and installed Shi Jingtang's Later Jin—making a subject into a sovereign. It was an upheaval without precedent.

sentences.zh: 金人效尤，而張邦昌、劉豫之事出焉。

translations.literal: The Jin people followed this bad example, and the affairs of Zhang Bangchang and Liu Yu emerged therefrom.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin followed that example, producing the affairs of Zhang Bangchang and Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 邦昌雖非本心，以死辭之，孰曰不可。

translations.literal: Bangchang, though not from his true mind, declined with death—who could say it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang was unwilling at heart and chose death rather than accept the throne. Who can fault him?

sentences.zh: 豫乘時徼利，金人欲倚以為功，豈有是理哉。

translations.literal: Yu seized the time to seek profit; the Jin wished to rely on him for achievement—how could there be such reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu seized the moment for private gain. The Jin hoped to use him for their ends—an arrangement doomed from the start.

sentences.zh: 撻懶初薦劉豫，後以陝西、河南歸宋，視猶儻來，初無固志以處此也。

translations.literal: Talan at first recommended Liu Yu; afterward he gave Shaanxi and Henan back to Song—regarding them still as casually come; from the start he had no steadfast will to handle this.
translations.idiomatic: Talan first backed Liu Yu, then ceded Shaanxi and Henan to Song as if they were windfalls he cared little to hold. He never had a firm purpose in any of it.

sentences.zh: 積其輕躁，終陷逆圖，事敗南奔，適足以實通宋之事爾，哀哉！

translations.literal: Accumulating his levity and rashness, he finally fell into a rebellious design; when affairs failed he fled south—just enough to substantiate the matter of communicating with Song, alas!
translations.idiomatic: His recklessness piled up until treason engulfed him. Flight south in defeat only confirmed what many had long suspected—that he had conspired with Song. Alas!
